text:
anna: quick question — can someone run a focused micro-alloc benchmark against the kv-cache eviction path? canary has been drifting up ~200MB over a 6h run, looks like fragmentation or slow free path. pinging @sam @maria :thinking_face:

sam: i can take this. what exact workload + seed?

anna: reproduce with `gpt-small-sim` workload, seq_len=1024, batch=8, latency-slo=150ms. important part: long lived connections (reuse kvcache) and burst churn every ~30s. aim to run for 2h to see steady state.

sam: ok running on a rtx-a5000 canary. i'll add jemalloc stats and periodic heapshots. command i'm using:
```bash
MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,background_thread:true \
REDWOOD_BENCH_WORKLOAD=gpt-small-sim \
./bench --seq 1024 --batch 8 --duration 7200 --kv-reuse=true \n```

maria: also capture pprof heap and tcmalloc-like allocation stacks if possible. if you're on jemalloc, `jeprof`/`jeheap` snapshots are useful. add `--heapshot=every:600` to get 10m interval dumps.

ci-bot: benchmark job queued: https://ci.redwood.local/job/bench/54321 (artifacts will appear under artifacts/54321/). ETA ~25m.

sam: first 40m result attached (uploaded to CI). quick summary: resident set grows ~120MB in first 30m then plateaus but RSS fragmentation increases. heapshot names: artifacts/54321/heapshot-0.heap, heapshot-1.heap, heapshot-2.heap

maria: looked at heapshot-2 quickly — lots of small freelist fragmentation around ~6KB/8KB buckets; free count low but internal frag high. suspect arena growth due to mixed-size allocations from HTTP connection + kvblocks. can you also capture per-thread stats? `jeprof --show_alloc` helps.

anna: good call. if it's fragmentation we can try forcing the slab-merge path or tune decay. what's the MALLOC_CONF you'd recommend for an experiment?

maria: try `MALLOC_CONF: decay_time:10,lg_dirty_mult:1,background_thread:true` to force faster purging and lower dirty pages. also try compile with CONFIG_MERGE_SMALL_SLABS=1 locally for an A/B.

eli: i can add a small regression test to perf suite that runs this microworkload for 45m and checks steady-state RSS delta < 50MB. assigning to myself, will push patch + CI job by EOD.

sam: re-run with maria's MALLOC_CONF and added per-thread jeprof. new job 54322 queued.

ci-bot: benchmark job queued: https://ci.redwood.local/job/bench/54322

sam: preliminary 54322: RSS delta reduced to ~30MB over 2h, fragmentation metric (internal_bytes/wired_bytes) down from 1.8 -> 1.05. looks promising. attaching flamegraph link: https://ci.redwood.local/artifacts/54322/flame.svg

anna: awesome — can we document the MALLOC_CONF change + recommended config in the runtime perf guide? if it helps, we should default this for canaries.

maria: agreed — i'll draft a short section with commands and rationale. also filing a follow-up issue to run the experiment across other instance types (A100, T4) to verify behavior.

eli: PR for perf test created: https://git.redwood.local/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/198 — includes CI job + pass criteria.

anna: thanks all. summary: run + heapshots showed small-bucket fragmentation, tuning decay/purge reduces RSS drift. next: validate across hw and consider default MALLOC_CONF for canaries. :white_check_mark:
